body: Gallium melts at about 29.8 °C, so a solid piece turns liquid in your palm. Yet this soft metal is the base of gallium arsenide and gallium nitride chips used in LEDs, lasers and power electronics.

scene_notes.caption:
GaAs and GaN make
special chip wafers.

tagline:
A METAL THAT MELTS.
A CHIP THAT SHINES.
